title: SCAM-NOT DEVELOPED BY SCIENTISTS
body:
2026 EDIT: app wanted to charge me and has so many hidden costs and subscriptions now. I cancelled the first time. Came back and found it was worse. Advertised as developed by researchers and university departments. They did this to pull in good reviews in the first year or two and then piled on the scams and the app is no longer useful due to all the pushing to download and sign up to their other apps where they can charge you hundreds in hidden sign ups when you join the “free” $1.49 AU trial without going through your Apple subscriptions. They do this to get your financial details and attach them to the free trials of all their other apps that you accept after the first payment. Make sure you check your fabulous account carefully and unsubscribe to each individual plan they attach to it. 

If you used an Apple forwarding email to hide your own email, copy the email address from the “acc verification” email you receive when signing up, and use that to sign in and cancel everything.

The entire app is automated AI. Even the one on one session is AI. Do not fall for it.

OLD REVIEW:
This app is beautiful, sound effects, graphics, storyline, regular interactions and messages for us on our journey, it’s more exciting and fulfilling than social media. After using Fabulous to actively work on my own health and goals, I don’t feel a need to check in on what everyone else is doing. The scientific research proves itself in this app, offering the regular hit of dopamine that social media creates, without all the tension and anxiety. I’m loving this app. Will retain it for as long as I’m able, even after the habits are established, it’s such a beautiful companion to my day, with morning and nightly 2min meditative coaching read to me, it keeps me focused on the here and now which is vital to health in our modern world.

title: Over priced, flashy, useless
body:
This app markets itself to neurodivergent folk who struggle with executive function.  It doesn’t let you choose your first goal, it forces you into a goal (that for me is the wrong task). Also, I’m autistic with a PDA profile and as such “demands” are an assault to my nervous system and actually cause a freeze.  I need choices not instructions. It’s infuriating. This app is less than useful, it’s harmful.  I want my money back.

After contacting their customer support, and finding them absolutely useless, I hope their clothes itch forever, their pens never work, their pencils always break, they stub their toes on every single uneven paver, their glasses are always blurry, their haircuts are always bad. I hope every time they have an important meeting they have visible snot on their nose, and food in their teeth and toilet paper on their shoes. 

They can go eff themselves.


UPDATE:  in May they refunded my money and cancelled my subscription.  Today they charged my account again and I will be 
having them charged with theft.

I emailed them three times to ask why they were charging my account.  They didn’t reply to a single one.  I contacted my bank and requested they retrieve my money and I’m so very mad.  The bank found other instances of them charging me that I had missed and retrieved them too..  on the 27th of May they told me my account was terminated and then charged me again on 6 June and 6/August.  This company is predatory.

title: Beautiful but distracting
body:
Beautiful UI, feature rich, think having a meditation app and & various life coaching apps in 1. But for me, I just want to build my routine with steps and timer so I can autopilot and not forget my next step. And it was hard to get back to the routine with so many popup windows, some video and animations took time to play, some guide/inspiration story/life lesson took forever to be dismissed, I have to click 10 times to get back to my routine. When you compete a simple step, the app insisted you have to take the reward with all the configrats and more slow animation. This combined with a lack of sleep night before and you got a morning routine full of frustration. The app thinks it is so smart that it had to inject its opinions and made so many decisions for me. Think auto suggested goal to build a habit when that habit already been in place. 
The routine building is also very clunky. I’m used to Apple reminders where all the items can be dragged up and down or edited as you see them. But with this app, you would have to click to edit, choose menu to edit habits, get to habit list in edit mode, then click on each habit. So many steps.
I find the life coaching is so very helpful for me, they are quite generic and not scientific based advice. Like a lovely story the grandmother tells the kids but not suitable for adults with challenges and real life concerns. I so want to like this app but it’s so frustrating that the app focus is on getting users to spend more time with the app than actually helping them getting on with their lives.

title: Not So Fabulous
body:
I subscribed to Fabulous on a trial basis for $25, on their website on the 15th of February. After about a week, I realised it wasn’t for me and to avoid paying for a full subscription for something I didn’t want, I cancelled.
On the 28th of February, the day my trial would have ended, I received an email from Fabulous confirming that my subscription was cancelled. 

However, when checking my bank balance that same day, I found $60.99 had be taken from my account by a Fabulous Paris. The exact cost of the full subscription, the same subscription I cancelled and received an email confirmation from Fabulous for. 

I contacted their email support and haven’t heard from them, nothing but cricket’s. Today is March 5th.

This is a warning that Fabulous doesn’t live up to the definition of the word they’ve used to name their service. Ignoring a cancellation, that they confirmed, then charging me the full price of a subscription anyway, is not Fabulous. It is better defined by the word Horrible. I’ve scratched their paint job and that word is what I found hiding on the layer beneath.

I am not going to chase Fabulous for a refund or fall to my knees and beg for one. I’ve already asked for a refund, as I wrote above; “I contacted their email support and haven’t heard from them, nothing but cricket’s”. That was March 5th; now it is March 9th and the only reply I’ve gotten is after writing of my experience with their product on a public page.

They’ve already got my refund request; writing on here and suggesting I try again is disgraceful. 

I received an email stating my subscription had been cancelled and then had $60.99 removed from account. Fabulous Paris has my refund request. They can show their colors and do what is right, or they can write me replies that suggest I haven’t even tried. Either choice is a direct insight into what Fabulous is all about. 
I’m standing my ground. They have my request, they can make their choice.

title: Taking money from my account
body:
19th Dec 2024 I looked at this app and the half way through the questionnaire I realised I cannot afford this. Sadly I must have gone too far through the process and they charged me.  I emailed them and was told I would not be charged.   

I have been charged monthly and have never used the app.  Getting help is impossible.  Once you find the request help form online, you are forced to only choose from selected problems that didn’t fit my issue.  The. You can only type 250 characters and 1 file.  

I got a response days later and all they did was refund me $2.99, said they have stopped the subscription and then closed the ticket. There was no opportunity for me to talk to someone to sort this out so I have had to do the same process again.  The money is still coming out of my account! I am in Australia and my bank cannot stop this from reoccurring but they can reverse each payment but I have to call them every month! 

In total they have taken approximately $140 from my account.  The transactions were only and got list in my statement with day to day living transactions until recently.  

I have adhd so that also didn’t help.  

I do not recommend this app for anyone, Let alone someone with ADHD!

title: Confusing interface
body:
Hi there. First, I appreciate the effort and intention of this app. The content and overall approach seems right. 

But after a few days I just couldn’t follow it all. The interface makes it confusing as to what is important. Habits were added without my awareness or consent. The “preparing the water” habit was added but removed. I couldn’t tell when I’d fully finished the habits for a day. The main screen is bloated with adds for other apps and I can’t remove it. There is no way to remove an afternoon routine given I already have an evening routine. 

It needs to be simple and logical. Stories and circles aren’t really explained and I don’t see how they add value. It’s trying to do too much for the user but it’s just overwhelming. I’d use this app if it were simplified and I could really see when I’d done everything and not be be forced to see adds. Thanks

After this didn’t work and I was charged the amount (which declined due to insufficient funds of my bank account), I was advised that prolonged failure to pay the subscription would default cancel the account and payment request. I waited for this to occur and once it did I deleted my account and consequently their rights to keep my data. However, 3 months on and I am still being continuously charged this amount and have had to ensure that it declines by not allowing more than $90 into my spending account. I couldnt find any way on the site to undo this so I wrote to the help centre, explaining that it was a mistake. They immediately responded: 

Hi there,

Thank you for reaching out to Fabulous. We've located the following subscription(s) associated with your email address xxxxx @xxxxx

Fabulous
Bundle Premium Bimonthly Plan + 14-day Free Trial
$79.99 AUD

Fabulous
Fabulous Premium Bimonthly Plan + 14-day Trial
$62.99 AUD

Unfortunately, none of these subscriptions contain charges that are eligible for a refund. You can visit this help article to learn more about your subscription(s) and how to cancel them if needed.

Best regards,
The Fabulous Member Care Team

title: Extremely dodgy
body:
I rarely review apps but this one needs to be called out. 

App pricing seemed reasonable in the App Store, and I downloaded it to try it out. As others have said, it’s intentionally designed to make you think you have to commit to a plan just to try it out. And the plan in the app was 4x the price of what it said in the App Store. Not good.

If you click and close that window, you then immediately get offered the app at a far lower price (pretty much the original advertised rate), albeit with a shorter free trial. But then if you select that like I did you start getting pestered straight away with offers of “upgrades”. All of this before you can even take a basic look at the app and see what it’s like.

After far too many pages, offers and prompts in the way of trying the app I decided to cancel. Only you can’t from within the app or the App Store. So from there I go to the (awful) website and cancel. Now I get offered an even lower price option and hassled not to cancel. As well as pages that look like you’ve cancelled, until you scroll down and find the “continue to cancel” button.

After you cancel you then get an email offer for a 30 day free trial instead of the original 2 weeks (then 1 week) offer.

Incredibly disingenuous, and an absolute mess. Looks very clearly designed to trick people into overpaying. Stay away.

title: This App changed my life!
body:
1st review: I’ll get right to the point, take it from someone who studied behavioural psychology a bit in their degree. This is practical, and based on science. If you’re determined enough, this app could help you become the person you aspire to be!

2nd review: This app has been my companion in my journey to a healthier life full of good habits! But as life gets more complex, I felt the need to provide feedback to the app developers. 

I understand the strength of a rigid routine that's defined by consistency and discipline. But this app has one downside given the new challenges I’ve faced. It allows for little flexibility in terms of adding things as you go (sort of like a calendar). 

Don’t get me wrong, I hate calendars! But I’d appreciate the ability to input my (one off) impulsive/weekend plans every now and then into the app! 

I seriously can’t wait to see something similar added to the app. Stay Fabulous!

title: Glitchy, Expensive and unhelpful
body:
This ap is way too expensive for how glitchy it is. I paid this exorbitant fee and never used it longer than the trial period anyway. Kept having to shutdown the ap and restart it because it freezes on various windows.

It’s far too expensive for something that didn’t change my day and was easy to stop using. Especially when there are plenty of free and fun aps that do a better job (check out finch). 

It’s also suss. During COVID lockdown I couldn’t buy groceries because I got trapped by the free one week trial trick (it’s not 7 days, it’s 6). I immediately contacted customer service to cancel (as soon as the money went from my account) and they couldn’t find any records, despite everything being done through iCloud, iPhone & App Store. I’m a digital native who understands subscriptions and this just never made any sense. 

Regardless, even though I’d paid for it I tried to force myself to use it and make the best of a situation. Couldn’t do it. This ap fell by the wayside within weeks. Many better alternatives have been developed, don’t waste your precious time or energy on this glitcher.

title: I LOVE this app, BUT…

For starters, there is no way to ‘favourite’ the coaching series or particular audios you find. You can download them, but there is no way to find your downloads?! Secondly, there is no search function? If I find a coaching series I like, I have to scroll through them all to find it again the next day. A search function would be SO helpful. I would really love to see a ‘favourite’ feature and an easier way to search and navigate between resources.

I used the app for a while then I stopped because I felt like the app added to the distractions I was trying to avoid. I came back to it months later when I was looking for something similar, only because I already paid for the premium. This time I’m enjoying it more, being there before I ignore the fluff and find the UI more manageable.

title: Great app- bad billing practices and service
body:
I want to love this app. I use it every day, and honestly get a lot out of it.  As an app goes, it’s brilliant, and very worthy of 5 stars.

However, it’s not just that. It’s a rather pricey app (which is fine), with very bad billing practices and errors. The turn around on any support enquiry is also about 7 days. 

I would still recommend it, but only if you are in the financial (and emotional) position to accommodate large billing errors with a lengthy fix time, and associated interruption to premium features.

Beautiful and well researched app, when the customer service and support can keep up it will be 5 stars.

title: Wouldn’t recommend this to anyone.
body:
I’ve never written an app review before, but I’ve never had such a negative experience with one. 

I downloaded this app to see what it was all about at the end of last year. The information on the app wasn’t anything new or different, and it was pointless in terms of value it added to my life. I’ve read books that I’ve borrowed for free from the library that have had a much greater impact on me. 

I cancelled my free trial prior to when the period ended - but last week I got an email saying they attempted to take the money anyway and it failed (luckily). I submitted an immediate appeal to prevent further charge attempts and was assured a response within the next few days. There has been none. 

The customer service is terrible from these guys and they give zero email updates regarding your account or payments. They proceeded to take the money from my account today, and as a uni student only working part time I cannot afford to pay for an app that I was led to believe I was no longer subscribed to. 

I have completed yet another ticket submission today, and this time hope to get a very prompt response. This poorly constructed app backed by non existent customer service is simply not worth it. 

Want to improve your life? Step outside, do some breathing, and put your phone away so you’re not at all tempted download this scam of an app.

This app is the best as you are just following it then it just became your habit without knowing it. I hate telling myself good things but I just put what I think of me by being loved for the sake of doing the challenge but it grows on me. I am not fully healed yet but this app is very helpful. Thank you developers! You did an amazing job specially the voice and the graphics. I hope you’ll put more graphics next time and put some white noise (rain noise) while listening to the motivational quotes.

Also this app provides you a morning couching and evening too which is the best. It gives me a positive morning and makes me feel okay before going to sleep. ♥️

title: Horrible design for those with ADHD
body:
I had this app previously and found it really useful for helping me stick with healthy habits, as I struggled with as someone with ADHD. This is the reason I decided to get it again. 

Unfortunately, changes that have been made since, which I’m pretty sure are purely around increasing engagement, include blocking the route to access your habits with a bunch of distracting tiles. I have used these features in the past and some are really good, however my primary purpose for accessing the app is to have a quick checklist of the habits I’m trying to maintain. 

Sometimes, I get so distracted I forgot why I even opened the app and then forget to check what habits I was meant to be doing, rendering the app useless in these situations. 

Ironically, this design probably is increasing engagement if you are only looking at metrics such as time spent in the app. Also ironically, I’m pretty sure habit forming apps are extremely popular with people with ADHD given issues with memory, organisation etc. in fact I just googled “adhd and habit forming apps” and you had the second ad space. 

For the love of god, please remove the distractions so people can use the app for its intended purpose.

title: An app that really needs to take a chill pill!
body: An okay idea for an app. For 3+ days, it kept bothering me multiple times about drinking water every morning. (I already do that, by the way! Didn’t think to ask?) At one point, it wanted me to put water by my bed, but when I told it no (because I don’t enjoy bumping it and spilling water everywhere in the middle of the night), it seemed worried that I wouldn’t drink water in the morning. Chill out, Fabulous app! I’m gonna be okay! And there’s just so much going on in the app screen at the same time… some affirmation video with poem, with different pop-up-type boxes around and tick boxes. Do I tick them? Oh wait… they don’t respond. Didn’t I already tick that? Does it want me to tick it again, or is that for tomorrow? Chill out, Fabulous app! You’re stressing ME out! So, yeah… I had to delete it. Nice try, though. I did want this to be good, because I think the underlying science is solid. I hope they can work out the interface bit.

I also think the options for notification sounds and music are very limited and the ones on the app I found quite annoying, so I will just keep it muted when using it.

The most frustrating thing was that with the timed tasks, the timer stopped working when you turned your phone off! I don’t leave my phone on while I am studying or writing ib my journal as I find it quite distracting so I think it would be better if this function would work without needing to keep your phone on (also uses a lot of power)

If these things were improved I think I would definitely use this app regularly and recommend it to others, but at the moment I don’t think is a useful app for me to use

Take care and do not buy into this very well marketed super creepy app!!

title: Please simplify the UX!
body: Hey guys, I find this app pretty hard to navigate and use. Simple is always better. So many pop ups and tooltips that don’t have a close button (meaning you have to wait until the copy appears, or go through the example steps even when you accidentally pressed it). Also having a pop up within a pop up is really hard to navigate and i can’t remember where certain content was or how to get back to there on another day. It’s also very hard to get to “yesterday” to check off items you forgot to check off. Sometimes within a routine I swipe and yesterday appears and sometimes it doesn’t. There’s nowhere on the page that indications that you can or how you can get to yesterday. In addition it would be nice to be able to get to yesterday on the homepage, so you can see all routines from yesterday at once. There is a LOT of stuff in this app and you have to go through so many steps to get to the content. I am too overwhelmed to even dive into other pages than the home page. To also get to your subscription level and find out how to unsubscribe you HAVE to add a full name, and a photo. This is pretty bad for privacy. People should have the choice whether they divulge this information. Also that you cannot cancel your subscription in app and that how to do this is so hard to find (styles like disclaimer text at the very bottom of a page). Help me to cancel my subscription, I don’t want to pay for this app! The visual design is beautiful but I think some further thought in UX and user flows would be amazing!!

title: truly is fabulous
body:
I think this app is gonna save lives. The amount of support you can get from one little post in the ‘circles’, or if you simply state « hey guys... i need some support/encouragement ».... there are many strangers out there who may be going through something similar to what you’re going through, and those strangers are there to bring you up with them as they pursue their journey to better themselves. 

and that’s the main thing that i think would be super beneficial to not only younger kids who may be struggling, but also teens growing up, and even adults in their busy lives. that together, you can personally work on yourself, while someone else is there to not only work on themselves but to help you too! and it also goes the other way - if you feel you have knowledge that you have learned from going through, for example, depression, you can reply to other’s posts and spread your wisdom. what may have helped you could possibly help someone else! 

overall, it’s a beautiful app, an incredibly effective way (by using routines) to help better myself and others, and i think i would 100% recommend it to anyone that may need a bit more good in their life. thank you so much <3

title: Overwhelming and confusing app to use
body:
I'm not one of those frustrated users wanting to leave a bad review beacue of a tiny broken feature. I've been using the paid version of the app for 2 years thinking it's a MVP and hoping it gets better. But, I was wrong. 

It seems the development team do not believe in user experience as there are so many features, mainly difficult to use. 
The simplest rule of thumb in UX is to have one primary action per screen with one secondary and in edge cases you can introduce the third action but in a very subtle way. And, in this app you can see a very busy UI with a handful of actions all seemed to be in primary style which makes the entire look and feel overwhelming and very difficult to communicate with.

I hope you'll invest a fraction of the money you're earning in user experience and do some user testing to understand your users and their needs!

To be perfectly honest, I can get most of the usable features you're offering free of charge elsewhere.

Lastly, I wanted to remind you why you built this app in the first place: to calm our mind and thoughts but I get the opposite from this app.

The habit building structure is a guidance and encouragement based system, which is great for people like me who need a little extra motivation.
Being able to add an event like moving house to the app that would interrupt some habits, and a bit of support for it would be great to see.
There is one "bedtime story", The Bronze Ring, purported to have the message that "it pays to be kind" that describes some gruesome and frankly not very kind acts committed by the "hero" without warning, which quite upset me when I listened to it. I won't be listening to that one again.

title: This is going to save my life
body:

This app can cater to everybody including all gender identities. If you’re working a full time job and juggling lots of responsibilities, or living with debilitating depression or chronic illness and spend your days in bed. This app will help you to improve your life through very small, achievable goals, that actually make a difference. Better yet, they are catered to what matters to you based on small quizzes. 

If you have the $5 per month, you can’t afford to lose by using this app. 

I do wish that when you ‘like’ a discover post, it would save somewhere. Also, some of the things you press on don’t have clear ways to exit them like a cross, some of the natural navigation could still be improved. 

This is an app to change your life.

title: Not worth the hype
body: Signed up for the 7-day trial premium, didn't get a confirmation of payment or of account creation and after a few days, tried to cancel my account. After searching on the website, I wasn't able to find their customer service details easily and when I did, I received an automated email back letting me know the inbox was unmonitored. I Googled 'the fabulous app customer service' and managed to find the TYPEFORM to get in contact with their customer service team. I requested a cancellation and it took them a few days to respond: they were very vague and weren't able to find my account. They told me to click on another 'magic link' to complete set-up (despite my PayPal reflecting the EUR1 that was already debited from my account). I tried to follow directions but to no avail, when I responded, it took another few days to receive another equally vague response. In that time after requesting cancellation, I was debited EUR39 (the full years' subscription). I finally gave up on their customer service, and took the matter up directly with PayPal: I blocked any further debits from The Fabulous and launched an unauthorised payment case against the EUR39. PayPal is refunding the money and I will never recommend The Fabulous to anyone. As someone who has worked for Saas companies, I can't believe how unfriendly the homepage is for customers who are wanting to log into their account. Customer service isn't a top priority for them either: a Typeform is just shocking-why not invest in a live chat extension? The App itself is tedious: the first goal is to drink water every day and you're constantly getting pop up recordings to help motivate you. Needless to say, it wasn't for me.

I do, however, think the pricing model needs a change up. 

I’ll be subscribing for 1 year - but would prefer a lifetime pass. At $400 it’s too much of an investment - and I don’t feel like it is a good deal - when apps sometimes disappear off the face of the planet with a couple years. 

1 year sub is more affordable, better cost vs risk - than other popular apps, but I would love to see the price lowered as adoption increases and the business is more viable - just because I think better, more affordable access to these kinds of tools would be a good thing for humanity in general. Not everyone can afford these things and it breaks my heart.

Wishful thinking I am sure - but I had to bring it up!

title: Meditation Music Doesn’t Simply Switch Off
body:
I thought I signed up for the 7 day trial, and then realised I had paid $62 for this app!
It was not obvious nor clear that the trial would result in an automated payment.

Anyway, so I enjoy the meditation aspect of it (that is why I gave this two stars).

However, when you want to finish meditation music EACH time, you have to tap out of it, then tap that you don’t want to invite friends to try the app, then tap anywhere....again!
And no one feels like doing that to simply turn off meditation music!

And if you try to avoid this process, it will snooze and start playing music later without warning- that you can’t switch off.

First world problems, right? Well when you’ve accidentally paid $62 for an app, the one aspect you enjoy is too clunky to turn off.

I’ve stopped using the app...and it has made me more aware of marketing techniques to get you to accidentally sign up.
I can see a lot of other people have also experienced this....which is unfortunate that type of app, on a moral ground, would be this way inclined.

title: !!! TRIGGERING APP !!!
body:
I started this app as a free trial. During the walk through of the app I received a “message from 2029 me”. It was saying I had changed my life and turned everything around because on this day I signed up for this app. It was kind of gimmicky and weird but I just kind of ignored it and kept exploring. After a bit I went into the app store to cancel my trial. I did this so I wouldn’t forget to later and accidentally get charged. A little bit after I did that I saw a notification from the app. It started with the same “It’s you from 2029” thing and I assumed it was just the same message from before, it was not. The next few lines said “I have not changed. I am still stuck in my bad habits. I am still the same person I was 9 years ago...” etc. Followed by something about, its not too late to change us - sign up for the app.

As someone who went on this app to maybe start implementing some good habits into my life, and start self-recovery from my mental illnesses, I found this message to be extremely triggering. Even though I know it wasn’t a message from “2029 me”, having someone present this idea to me that I would never get better? Extremely destructive and confronting to read. I have been struggling with depression, an eating disorder, anxiety, and body dysmorphia, for a long time, and am trying to recover. I thought a self-help/motivation app would be a good, small, first step to take on my journey. Instead I was confronted with the idea I would never get better - all for these people to promo the sale of their app. I don’t understand why they would use negative and destructive messages to, scare people into buying their app? Rather than positive reinforcement and kind words for people who actually want/are trying to get better but are struggling. 

Just because I know the message was fake doesn’t mean it didn’t impact me, now I have doubts running around in my head, that I know are irrational and untrue but are still there. And were put there by this manipulative app. Very upsetting that the creators of this app clearly just want money, and they use confrontational, in-your-face, and destructive methods to obtain that.

title: Motivating and Fabulous and Fun!
body: Loving Fabulous so far! Within just the first week of use it’s motivated me to drink water upon waking and have a nice healthy energy-lifting breakfast for an efficient day ahead. I love how it gives you the option to take things slow if you (like me) struggle with organisation and routine and staying focused. It doesn’t throw a bunch of tasks at you in one big clump. It gives you the option of adding daily tasks when your feeling more confident in doing so and, once you’ve finished your first task of drinking water upon waking for 3 consistent days, you can then start doing weekly challenges which are used to help you complete actions that you normally struggle with (such as exercising, meditation and creativity). I’ve noticed that it has also improved my sleep because I’m not spending time lying awake anxious about what I’m going to be doing the next day. It’s improved the symptoms of my ADD as organisation, staying focused and procrastination has always been a HUGE problem for me. These problems have always caused lots of anxiety, thus this is also great for anyone dealing with anxiety or depression. This app makes routine fun and gets you motivated! It’s worth every penny and deserves all the hype! Thanks to the team that invented this app! You are quite literally a life-saver.

title: Frustrating, useless app
body:
I thought I’d give this app a go despite the hefty $60 monthly fee and extremely short one week trial. I signed up for the free trial but realised within minutes that it wasn’t for me. It was ridiculously difficult to use, hard to figure out where anything was or what to do with it, and just the most frustrating app I have ever tried. Also, the first and only tip it gave me was to drink water. Seriously?! I don’t need to pay $60 for an app to remind me to drink water.
I immediately decided to get out of the trial but I could not for the life of me find the settings part of the app, or anywhere that I could cancel it. Long video pop-ups kept appearing and I couldn’t dismiss them. I eventually got so frustrated that I deleted the app, wrongly assuming this would cancel my trial.
You can imagine my annoyance when I noticed $60 had come out of my account a week later. I looked at the app again and STILL couldn’t find out how to get out of the trial. I tried to send a complaint and to get my money back but even that process was annoying, with emails bouncing back and annoying hoops to jump through. These people don’t want to be contacted. I then received a reply about a month later saying they wouldn’t give my money back.
LUCKILY, I had also complained to Apple support and they were kind enough to refund my money and cancel my membership with the app.
A very annoying experience overall. I definitely don’t recommend this app. There are soo many free or cheap self-help apps that are so much better.

title: You don’t *have* to sign up for the 7-day trial
body:
Lots of reviews here from people complaining about being charged a subs fee or not cancelling in time. If you’re just checking out the app to see whether it’s for you, DON’T press that big, bright button when you get to the 7-day trial splash screen. Instead, look for the discreet cross at top left of the splash screen and tap on that. This will cancel the splash page and allow you to continue the set-up process as a free user. Once beyond that, all the paid options are clearly indicated and optional. 

It’s disingenuous of the app makers to design a set-up process that funnels users into signing up for the trial, making it look like this is the *only* option. Continuing with the completely free version (no subscription and no trial) should be a clearly indicated alternative for newcomers. If the app is good enough and its locked features appealing enough, users will want to try the subscription option anyway. As it is, the subtle trickery leaves a bad taste. And that’s a pity given the care and imagination that appears to have gone into the app’s features. 

Another criticism: on first opening this app plays strident music. That is, before you’ve had a chance to change any internal settings. That’s just bad form. Especially for an app focused on wellbeing. Surely the makers are aware that random, unwanted music is not conducive to calmness of mind and general wellbeing?

Besides the pay wall for the premium version (which I haven’t used and can’t comment on - the free version has ALWAYS met my needs thusfar) and possible health kit integration (Especially for activity/health tracking and mental health (very important)) - which will hopefully he updated in a future release very soon (hi developers: hint hint 😬), This app is top notch. 

Highly, highly recommended 😍

title: Money Grab
body:
This app is a joke. I accepted the $70 charge for 12 months thinking it will unlock the full app. 

NO, it doesn’t! 

Most features are still locked and the app is pretty limited and useless for $70.

Now it informs me that for a further $135 I can unlock the “premium” features. 

Just a dirty sales tactic to make a $205 price tag seem cheaper that it really is.

Another dishonest sales tactic is displaying a monthly price, and claiming you can cancel any time.

NO! You get charged upfront for the full 12 months, and if you cancel after a month, too bad, you’ve paid for the full 12 months. You’re only canceling the next 12-month renewal.

Deceptive.

title: No support
body:
I purchased the early subscription of this app. I really loved the concept the art and everything else. 

However in the first week it presented malfunctions in the badge notifications.
And the most interesting thing is that in one of the letters was advocated the importance of the ‘notification philosophy’ that the software uses, only when necessary to not compromise the user’s experience. 

I messaged the support, but there was no answer. I waited one week, tried to fix it myself by deleting and reinstalling the app but the stuck badge app was still there.

In the process of reinstalling, I lost the progress that I’ve made in the app. 

They don’t have a simple account login or information recovery... so every time you restore for some issue, you lose your progress on the tasks.

I tried to message the support team again, this time not only to recover my progress but also to solve the stuck red badge.
After a week there was no answer!

I’m not willing to pay a year subscription of more than 70 $Aud for an app which has no support. 

Specially if you advocate for more conscious notifications but can’t care less for issues regarding your app.

And you talk about motivation but if I lose my progress, how can I be motivated to start over? Why don’t you have a simple account login and store information on my iCloud or something?

Disappointing.

Edit: after hunting through the settings, I found you can disable all sounds. I recommend turning all these off before you start using the app because otherwise they override your phone’s silent function.

title: Just What I Needed 🌱💜
body:
I don’t usually bother to review apps, but I’ve only been using fabulous a few days and I can already see it making a ‘fabulous’ difference in my life!
Overall I’m simply thrilled with the app.

However, there are a few features I’d love to see added. One of these is an easier way to make a repeating action throughout the day; something to regularly remind you to drink water or take a moment to breathe, or another action. It’s technically already possible to do this, but only through making a long list of alarms. I’d just love to see a simpler and more visually appealing way to do this. Maybe also make it so these repeated actions move down through the list of of rituals throughout the day, so they’re always in the order you should next complete them. 
As well as this, it would be wonderful to have a way to personalise the app just a little, particularly more in visual terms. Maybe be able to upload your own pictures as a backgrounds, or a night mode for the whole app.

In all, these are mainly minor tweaks, the app is already so gorgeous and easy to use, I’ll be sure to recommend it to everyone I know!
Thank you endlessly!
